method: Fresh independent read-only audit of all 109 deployment and all 63 tooling/documentation paths in the frozen round-15 assignment. Review began after the freeze; the before-check independently read all 1,901 raw file bytes and compared SHA-256 values, and invoked the canonical exported snapshot() from scripts/snapshot.mjs using the pinned Node v24.22.1. Manually read every assigned source module, shell/Python/JavaScript/Go script, workflow/configuration, regression test/probe, and prose document in full. Traced installation and host identity reservations, immutable releases and control updates, service permissions and root/native/gateway ownership, source and build acquisition, native/DNS provenance, offline build isolation and resource bounds, provider/system configuration, secret handling, HTTPS configuration/certificate health/DNS renewal boundaries, stop/barrier/checkpoint ordering, rollback and interrupted recovery, request journals/spool lifetime and uncertain outcomes, workspace file/index/commit/worktree recovery and retained material. Compared stopped backup/restore and operator maintenance runbook commands with the actual implementation. Read all deployment regression/probe implementations without executing them. Traced source inventory, audit/full-test authorization (the user requires two clean rounds rather than the repository default three), exact targeted selection, environment sanitization, Linux/Windows/root execution, case-level reconciliation, Go/native acquisition and isolated verification, pinned workflows, and release tooling/documentation. Read the 19 ordinary feature-evidence JSON files fully as historical source documentation only; did not open linked prior audit reports or treat recorded passing outcomes as current proof. For the large capability JSON, read all 50 group assessments, all 178 method-to-workflow mappings and all 15 additional workflow assessments, then traversed every value and structurally/semantically checked method uniqueness and exact current TypeScript/JSON protocol coverage, classifications and counts, group bidirectional references, schema variant bindings, all 559 source-reference records, and explicit acceptance limitations. Parsed every nonblank line of pnpm-lock.yaml with duplicate-key/unsupported-syntax rejection and analyzed all 336 package/snapshot records, all 644 dependency edges and complete reachability, exact manifest importers/overrides, pinned versions and SHA-512 formats, Node compatibility, required/optional peer ranges and optional platform acquisition records. Parsed all 1,510 go.sum rows, checked uniqueness, module/version/hash formats and module/go.mod pairing, and verified all 166 current go.mod requirements including pinned Caddy/AliDNS have both required hashes. This was structural/semantic dependency analysis, not merely digest checking and not a fresh vulnerability feed or fetched-artifact verification. Completed the source review before the final integrity check. Re-read all 1,901 raw files and invoked the canonical exported snapshot() again with pinned Node: every hash, exact inventory name and digest remained unchanged. No source changes, old-checkout/history inspection, prior audit report inspection, full-suite execution, remote operation, or live integration was performed.
limitations: Read-only source audit. No tests or candidate reproductions were executed; local checks parsed current source data and verified integrity only.

No live Linux/systemd installation, service switch/rollback, cross-UID process proof, native CLI acceptance, ACME issuance/renewal, AliDNS API call, external provider/account/OAuth/MCP integration, paid inference, browser deployment, or network build/download was executed. These are unexecuted integrations, not skipped assigned source scope.

Historical feature evidence was assessed for claims, references and limitations only; its pass statuses, source hashes, prior audit links and report references were not used as correctness proof for this frozen snapshot.
Locked dependency graph structure, pinning and acquisition paths were reviewed; no external vulnerability database, upstream remote artifact or transparency service was queried.
